answer: Each agent commits an epoch-locked state root: a unique Blake3 hash over a 64 GB RAM array seeded by onyx, nectar and mirror, published before the epoch opens. The verifier issues random offsets; the agent must return the cache-line values within 40 ms, proving the array is resident in local memory rather than recomputed or shared. One honest agent holds one 64 GB array costing about $180; 10 fakes must hold 10 distinct 640 GB arrays, scaling cost linearly. Peers re-check the log of roots and responses; mismatched or late proofs slash the bond and freeze repeat offenders.
